## Goal and revision made before choosing a rule

On **2026-10-11**, the primary target was changed to cumulative error over the
available post-period window, before any rule was chosen and before half B was
opened for evaluation. This document loads **only half A**. The seed (2032026),
size stratification and saved county assignment are unchanged. Half B remains
reserved for confirmation after a rule is recorded by hand.

```{r setup}
# Load physically separate A inputs; assert the split before computing any statistics.
root<-normalizePath(getwd())
while(!file.exists(file.path(root,'_quarto.yml'))) {
 p<-dirname(root);if(p==root)stop('Repository not found');root<-p
}
source(file.path(root,'R/heldout_analysis.R'))
source(file.path(root,'R/backdate_helpers.R'))
source(file.path(root,'R/heldout_exploration.R'))
library(ggplot2)
input<-file.path(root,'data/derived/heldout/half_A_available.rds')
if(!file.exists(input)) stop('Run Rscript R/heldout_prepare.R first.')
obj<-readRDS(input)
stopifnot(all(obj$rows$half=='A'),sum(obj$rows$half!='A')==0,
 identical(obj$assignment_md5,unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(root,'data/derived/heldout/county_assignment.rds')))))
report_started<-proc.time()[['elapsed']]
min_k<-as.integer(params$min_k_average);stopifnot(min_k %in% 1:5)
d<-derive_exploration_A(obj$rows,min_k);z<-d$rows
out<-file.path(root,'_output/heldout/exploration/available_window');dir.create(out,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
write_table<-function(x,name) fwrite(x,file.path(out,paste0(name,'.csv')))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width=13,fig.height=9)
```

The original split uses quintiles of mean pre-period expected counts from saved
main TWFE MAR fits, with ID tie-breaking and a separate missing-size stratum.
Models were fit on all counties; the split changes evaluation only. This snapshot
contains `r nrow(obj$manifest)` of `r obj$expected_groups` checkpoints. The old input
and output files remain preserved; revised exports are in `available_window/`.

## Saved data, targets and predictive coverage

County checkpoints store `sim`, `id`, `x`, `scenario`, `model`, `y_post`,
`mu_post_mean`, `mu_ho_mean`, `mu_ho_var`, and held-out predictive tails. There is
no post-period variance or predictive interval in those collapsed checkpoints.
The saved main fits contain per-year `y`, `y0_hat` and `y0_post_1`–`y0_post_200`,
with county `i`, simulation `r`, calendar `year` and true `start_year_sim`.
Event time is `year - start_year_sim`.

For event years 0–4, keep years with finite observed counts, finite predicted
means and strictly positive means. Let **k** be their count. For k ≥ 1:

- `err_raw = abs(sum(y) - sum(mu))`;
- `err_z = err_raw / sqrt(sum(mu))`.

Errors can cancel across years: this is the absolute error of the cumulative
count, not the average or sum of yearly absolute errors. Available windows need
not be contiguous; k records their length. `h0_raw`/`h0_z` use event year 0 only.
`k5_raw`/`k5_z` reproduce the original complete five-year targets, including the
original allowance for zero yearly point means. Secondary `average_raw` and
`average_z` average the respective available-window errors per county/model/scenario,
using only simulations with **k ≥ `r min_k`**. They are explanatory targets of
systematic prediction difficulty, include the current simulation when eligible,
and still contain sampling noise. Counts behind each average are saved. The old complete-window averages are retained
as `average_k5_raw` and `average_k5_z` sensitivities. An averaged county target can
label a simulation with no currently observable post year; such rows form a
separate k = 0 stratum for the explanatory analysis.

The stored `y0_post_*` are latent expected-count draws. Preparation adds independent
Poisson observation noise conditional on each saved draw, then sums predictive
counts over exactly the same usable years, preserving latent dependence through
the shared draw index. The interval uses empirical 2.5%/97.5% quantiles (R type 7).
It is not an interval obtained by adding yearly quantiles. If any of the saved
latent draws or generated predictive counts for a window is invalid, its coverage is unavailable; point-error
targets remain usable. Predictive-generation seeds are fixed and separate from
the unchanged assignment seed; no model is refitted. Per-year quantiles alone
are rejected by preparation.

```{r availability}
# Include k=0 explicitly; counts/shares use all pseudo-treated A county rows.
counts<-z[,.(rows=.N,old_complete_rows=sum(is.finite(k5_raw)),new_available_rows=sum(k>=1),
 old_counties=uniqueN(id[is.finite(k5_raw)]),new_counties=uniqueN(id[k>=1]),
 coverage_available=sum(is.finite(coverage))),by=.(scenario,model)]
write_table(counts,'row_counts');knitr::kable(counts)
kd<-z[,.N,by=.(scenario,model,k)]
kd[,share:=N/sum(N),by=.(scenario,model)]
write_table(kd,'k_distribution');knitr::kable(kd,digits=3)
write_table(d$averages,'county_average_targets')
knitr::kable(d$averages[,.(counties=.N,with_average=sum(n_average_raw>0),
 min_R=min(n_average_raw),median_R=median(n_average_raw),max_R=max(n_average_raw)),by=.(scenario,model)])
```

## Complete-window sensitivity: acceptance check

The old targets are retained as sensitivities. Each new k5 value is checked
against the saved old totals during preparation. This table independently checks
diagnostic/target eligible counts and mean baseline errors against the old formulas;
matching is required to three decimals. Diagnostic availability is held fixed
for this check, so an updated set of predictive tails cannot change its denominator.

```{r old-target-check}
check<-rbindlist(lapply(names(diagnostic_labels),function(diag)
 rbindlist(lapply(c('raw','z'),function(version) {
 old<-if(version=='raw') 'old_realized_raw' else 'old_realized_standardized'
 new<-paste0('k5_',version)
 z[,{
 eligible_old<-is.finite(get(diag))&is.finite(get(old));eligible_new<-is.finite(get(diag))&is.finite(get(new))
 list(diagnostic=diag,target=version,old_n_eligible=sum(eligible_old),new_n_eligible=sum(eligible_new),
 old_baseline_error=mean_finite(get(old)[eligible_old]),new_baseline_error=mean_finite(get(new)[eligible_new]))
 },by=.(scenario,model,sim)]
 }))))
stopifnot(all(check$old_n_eligible==check$new_n_eligible),
 all(sprintf('%.3f',check$old_baseline_error)==sprintf('%.3f',check$new_baseline_error)))
write_table(check,'k5_acceptance_by_simulation')
knitr::kable(check[,.(simulations=.N,count_match=all(old_n_eligible==new_n_eligible),
 baseline_match=all(sprintf('%.3f',old_baseline_error)==sprintf('%.3f',new_baseline_error))),by=.(scenario,model)])
```

## Associations stratified by window length

Scores are absolute diagnostics, except predictive surprise is `1 - p_two`.
Compute Spearman correlation, AUC and top-decile labels within
**scenario × model × simulation × k**. The target boundary uses all finite targets
in the stratum, before diagnostic availability is applied; include boundary ties.
Skip strata with fewer than five usable rows or a single outcome class. Constant
scores make correlations unavailable. Weight valid k statistics by their usable
stratum sizes, then average equally across simulations. The pooled, unstratified
version is shown alongside. Explanatory averaged targets can also be evaluated in a separate k = 0 stratum.

Every simulation-averaged statistic has MC SE `sd(statistic)/sqrt(n_sims)` using
finite simulations only; this is simulation Monte Carlo uncertainty, not an
independence assumption about repeated county rows. Tables display mean (MC SE).

```{r associations}
a<-exploration_associations(z)
write_table(a$per_k,'associations_per_k');write_table(a$per_sim,'associations_per_simulation')
stratum_n<-mc_summary(a$per_k,'n',c('scenario','model','diagnostic','target','k'))
write_table(stratum_n,'association_stratum_sizes')
knitr::kable(stratum_n[target=='err_z' & diagnostic %in% c('pre_rmse','ho_uncertainty','p_two'),.(scenario,model,diagnostic,k,n=n_display,n_sims=n_n_sims)])
associations<-mc_summary(a$per_sim,c('spearman','auc'),c('scenario','model','diagnostic','target','evaluation'))
write_table(associations,'associations_summary')
knitr::kable(associations[,.(scenario,model,diagnostic,target,evaluation,
 correlation=spearman_display,AUC=auc_display,n_sims=auc_n_sims)])
```

## Held-out predictive calibration

Mid-p splits equality probability evenly between the lower and upper tails.
Two-sided `p_two = min(1, 2 * min(p_upper, p_lower))`. Paired legacy inclusive
tails are converted exactly; a single tail is never guessed. The uniform reference
is a diagnostic benchmark: discrete mid-p and two-sided probabilities are not
exactly uniform even for a correctly specified count model. Departures from alpha
therefore describe tail behavior rather than proving miscalibration.

```{r calibration}
calibration<-rbindlist(lapply(c(.01,.05,.10),function(alpha)
 z[,.(alpha=alpha,n_available=sum(is.finite(p_two)),observed_share=mean_finite(as.numeric(p_two<alpha)),
 expected_share=alpha),by=.(scenario,model,sim)]))
calibration[,excess:=observed_share-expected_share]
write_table(calibration,'calibration_per_simulation')
cs<-mc_summary(calibration,c('observed_share','excess'),c('scenario','model','alpha','expected_share'))
write_table(cs,'calibration_summary');knitr::kable(cs[,.(scenario,model,alpha,observed=observed_share_display,expected_share,excess=excess_display)])
print(ggplot(z[is.finite(p_two)],aes(p_two))+geom_histogram(binwidth=.05,boundary=0)+
 facet_grid(model~scenario)+theme_bw()+labs(x='Two-sided held-out mid-p',y='County/simulation rows'))
```

## Retention curves, missing diagnostics and random baseline

Screens remain **per model**. Sweep the specified p-value grid, absolute standardized
error cutoffs 1–4 by 0.25, and pre-RMSE top 2.5%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% comparator.
Pre-RMSE ranks are within scenario/model/simulation, over finite diagnostics;
flag the nearest requested number of counties, with county ID breaking ties.
The requested 10% comparator is per model, whereas the legacy manuscript code
pooled pre-RMSE across models before screening.

For every screen evaluate **missing = keep** and **missing = exclude**, with the
missing share reported over all pseudo-treated rows. Error denominators are finite
target rows; coverage denominators additionally require a valid predictive interval.
Unavailable coverage is counted separately. Threshold equality is retained.
Random screening excludes exactly the same number of eligible counties, using
100 seeded permutations per simulation. Per-simulation 2.5%/97.5% random-reduction
quantiles are saved; the plotted band averages those quantiles across simulations.
It is a random-screening reference band, not a confidence interval for the mean.

```{r retention}
rules<-exploration_rules();write_table(rules,'rule_grid')
r<-exploration_retention(z,rules)
write_table(r$per_sim,'retention_per_simulation');write_table(r$size,'flag_rates_per_simulation')
key<-c('scenario','model','diagnostic','cutoff','rule_type','missing_handling','target')
values<-c('excluded_share','retained_share','baseline_error','retained_error','reduction','retained_coverage','random_mean','random_lo','random_hi','missing_share','n_retained','n_retained_coverage','coverage_missing_share')
retained<-mc_summary(r$per_sim,values,key)
write_table(retained,'retention_summary')
knitr::kable(retained[target %in% c('err_z','err_raw'),.(scenario,model,diagnostic,cutoff,missing_handling,target,
 retained=retained_share_display,reduction=reduction_display,coverage=retained_coverage_display,missing=missing_share_display)])
for(target_name in c('err_z','err_raw')) for(policy in c('keep','exclude')) {
 p<-ggplot(retained[target==target_name & missing_handling==policy],aes(excluded_share,reduction,color=diagnostic,group=diagnostic))+
 geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=random_lo,ymax=random_hi,fill=diagnostic),alpha=.1,color=NA)+
 geom_line(aes(y=random_mean),linetype='dashed')+geom_line()+geom_point(size=.8)+
 facet_grid(model~scenario)+theme_bw()+labs(title=paste(target_name,'— missing =',policy),x='Excluded share',y='Relative reduction in mean error')
 print(p);ggsave(file.path(out,paste0('retention_',target_name,'_',policy,'.png')),p,width=13,height=9,dpi=150)
}
```

## Model ranking and retained predictive coverage

Rank models by equally simulation-averaged retained mean error, separately for
raw/standardized cumulative and h0 targets. Lower error has lower rank; retain
ties. Baseline ranks use all finite unscreened target rows, not a diagnostic-specific
complete-case subset. Coverage always uses cumulative predictive counts over the
same observed window. The per-model retained populations may differ.

```{r rankings}
baseline<-r$per_sim[,.(baseline_error=mean_finite(baseline_error)),by=.(scenario,model,sim,target)]
baseline_summary<-mc_summary(baseline,'baseline_error',c('scenario','model','target'))
write_table(baseline_summary,'unscreened_baseline')
ranked<-rank_retention_A(retained,baseline_summary);write_table(ranked,'model_rankings')
knitr::kable(ranked[target=='err_z',.(scenario,model,diagnostic,cutoff,missing_handling,
 mean_error=retained_error_display,coverage=retained_coverage_display,retained=retained_share_display,
 unscreened_rank,retained_rank,ranking_changed)])
```

## Flag rates by original county-size stratum

The original size strata 1–5 and missing-size stratum 6 are unchanged. The tables
show simulation-averaged flag and diagnostic-missing rates with MC SE, for each
model/scenario/screen and both missing policies.

```{r size}
size<-mc_summary(r$size,c('flag_rate','missing_share'),c('scenario','model','diagnostic','cutoff','rule_type','missing_handling','stratum'))
write_table(size,'flag_rates_by_size')
knitr::kable(size[,.(scenario,model,diagnostic,cutoff,missing_handling,stratum,flag_rate=flag_rate_display,missing=missing_share_display)])
```

## Robustness across scenarios

The worst reduction is the **minimum** over the three scenarios; the worst coverage
is also the minimum. Missing scenario estimates prevent a claimed three-scenario
worst case. Scenario means and their MC SE are exported in the same table. No
standard error is assigned to the selected minimum itself.

```{r robustness}
robust<-dcast(retained,target+model+diagnostic+cutoff+rule_type+missing_handling~scenario,
 value.var=c('reduction','reduction_mc_se','retained_coverage','retained_coverage_mc_se'))
robust[,worst_reduction:=apply(.SD,1,function(v) if(all(is.finite(v))) min(v) else NA_real_),
 .SDcols=paste0('reduction_',c('MAR','Latent level','Latent trend'))]
robust[,worst_coverage:=apply(.SD,1,function(v) if(all(is.finite(v))) min(v) else NA_real_),
 .SDcols=paste0('retained_coverage_',c('MAR','Latent level','Latent trend'))]
write_table(robust,'scenario_robustness');knitr::kable(robust[target=='err_z'],digits=3)
```

## Common-sample sensitivity: intersection across all six models

The operational rule is still per model. This sensitivity intersects the six
per-model retention screens within each simulation, then also pairs finite target
availability across all six models. Error means and ranks use identical county
sets. Coverage availability can still differ by model and is reported through
its denominator. Compare these results with the per-model retained populations above.

```{r intersection}
common<-common_sample_A(z,rules);write_table(common,'common_sample_per_simulation')
common_summary<-mc_summary(common,values,key);write_table(common_summary,'common_sample_summary')
common_ranked<-rank_retention_A(common_summary,baseline_summary)
comparison<-merge(common_ranked[,.(scenario,model,diagnostic,cutoff,rule_type,missing_handling,target,
 common_error=retained_error,common_error_mc_se=retained_error_mc_se,common_coverage=retained_coverage,
 common_coverage_mc_se=retained_coverage_mc_se,common_rank=retained_rank)],
 ranked[,.(scenario,model,diagnostic,cutoff,rule_type,missing_handling,target,
 per_model_error=retained_error,per_model_coverage=retained_coverage,per_model_rank=retained_rank)],by=key)
write_table(comparison,'common_sample_comparison');knitr::kable(comparison[target=='err_z'],digits=3)
```

`target_definition`, `missing_diagnostic_handling`, `date`, and `rationale`.
The template remains blank. Record whether the diagnostic is a p-value, an absolute

Half-B confirmation must implement this same target and missing policy before use;
its intersection-sample section is currently a placeholder and was not run.
